(18 August) |longest wins = |longest unbeaten = |longest losses = |prevseason=[[2019 Ecuadorian Serie A|2019]] |nextseason=[[2021 Ecuadorian Serie A|2021]] }} The '''2020 Campeonato Ecuatoriano de Fútbol Serie A''' (until 18 September 2020 officially known as the '''LigaPro Banco Pichincha 2020''' for sponsorship reasons){{Cite web|url=https://www.primicias.ec/noticias/jugada/liga-profesional-pierde-patrocinador-banco-pichincha/|title=Banco Pichincha deja de ser el patrocinador de la Liga Profesional|date=18 September 2020|website=Primicias.ec|language=es|access-date=21 September 2020}} was the 62nd season of the [[Ecuadorian Serie A|Serie A]], Ecuador's top tier [[association football|football]] league, and the second under the management of the Liga Profesional de Fútbol del Ecuador (or '''LigaPro'''). [[Delfín S.C.|Delfín]] were the defending champions.{{Cite web|url=https://www.eluniverso.com/deportes/2019/12/15/nota/7647203/vivo-delfin-vs-liga-quito-final-campeon-liga-pro-2019|title=Delfín SC, campeón de la Liga Pro al vencer en penales a Liga de Quito|date=15 December 2019|website=El Universo|language=es|access-date=17 December 2019}} [[Barcelona S.C.|Barcelona]] won their 16th domestic league title after defeating [[L.D.U. Quito|LDU Quito]] 3–1 on penalties following a 1–1 draw on aggregate score in the finals. The competition was suspended from 14 March to 14 August due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Ecuador|COVID-19 pandemic]]. ==Format== The format for the 2020 season was decided by LigaPro's Council of Presidents on 22 October 2019. For this season, the league returned to the three-stage system used before the [[2019 Ecuadorian Serie A|2019 season]], scrapping the play-off stage played in the previous season.{{cite web|url=https://www.elcomercio.com/deportes/futbol-ligapro-formato-campeonato-2020.html|title=La LigaPro cambió el formato del campeonato nacional del 2020|language=es|publisher=El Comercio|date=22 October 2019|access-date=24 December 2019}} The first and second stages were played as single round-robin tournaments with all teams playing each other once for a total of 15 matches per stage. The first stage fixture was reversed for the second stage, and the top teams at the end of each stage qualified for the finals as well as the [[2021 Copa Libertadores|Copa Libertadores group stage]]. The finals were a double-legged series between the winners of both stages with a penalty shoot-out deciding the champion in case of a tie in points and goals scored. In case a team won both stages of the season, the finals would not have been played and that team would win the championship. An aggregate table including the matches of both the first and second stages was used to decide international qualification and relegation, with the best two teams (other than the stage winners) qualifying for the Copa Libertadores, and the next best three teams qualifying for the [[2021 Copa Sudamericana|Copa Sudamericana]]. The remaining Copa Sudamericana berth would have been allocated through the 2020 [[Copa Ecuador]], which was cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic and had its berth reallocated to the next best team in the aggregate table. Meanwhile, the teams that ended in the 15th and 16th place of the aggregate table would have competed in relegation play-offs against the third- and fourth-placed teams of the [[2020 Ecuadorian Serie B|2020 Serie B]] for the right to remain in the top tier for the following season,{{cite web|url=https://ligapro.ec/post/1025-detalles-fixture-2020.html|title=Detalles Fixture 2020|language=es|publisher=LigaPro|date=20 December 2019|access-date=24 December 2019|archive-date=23 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191223171402/https://ligapro.ec/post/1025-detalles-fixture-2020.html|url-status=dead}} however, in a Council of Presidents session held on 23 May 2020 it was decided not to expand the Serie A to 18 teams for the [[2021 Ecuadorian Serie A|2021 season]], meaning that the bottom two teams of the aggregate table at the end of the season were relegated to Serie B.{{cite web|url=https://www.eluniverso.com/deportes/2020/05/23/nota/7849899/ligapro-definidos-clubes-series-b|title=LigaPro definió no incrementar clubes en serie A para temporada del 2021|language=es|publisher=El Universo|date=23 May 2020|access-date=12 December 2020}} ==Teams== ===Stadia and locations=== {{location map+ |Ecuador |float=right |width=350 |caption=Locations of the 2020 Serie A teams. |places= {{location map~ |Ecuador |lat=-1.244866 |long=-78.623184 |label=

the COVID-19 pandemic== On 14 March 2020 after two Matchday 5 games had been played, the competition was suspended indefinitely by LigaPro due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Ecuador|COVID-19 pandemic]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.elcomercio.com/deportes/futbol-ecuador-quinta-fecha-suspension.html|title=La LigaPro suspende indefinidamente los campeonatos de fútbol de Serie A y Serie B en Ecuador|website=El Comercio|language=es|date=14 March 2020}} On 20 May LigaPro's Council of Presidents decided to tentatively resume the league on 17 July pending final approval by the Ecuadorian government, with matches to be played behind closed doors.{{Cite web|url=https://www.elcomercio.com/deportes/torneo-ligapro-volvera-disputarse-julio.html|title=El campeonato ecuatoriano de fútbol volverá a disputarse desde el 19 de julio|website=El Comercio|language=es|date=20 May 2020|access-date=8 June 2020}} That same day the Council approved to restart training activities on 8 June, which was later moved to 10 June per decision by the National Emergency Operations Committee (COE).{{Cite web|url=http://www.teleamazonas.com/2020/06/futbol-ecuatoriano-entrenamientos/|title=Fútbol ecuatoriano: COE Nacional autoriza el retorno de clubes a entrenamientos|website=Teleamazonas|language=es|date=4 June 2020|access-date=8 June 2020|archive-date=8 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200608174402/http://www.teleamazonas.com/2020/06/futbol-ecuatoriano-entrenamientos/|url-status=dead}} However, the date for the resumption of the competition was pushed back as the protocol approved by the Ecuadorian government through the National COE had set 29 July as the earliest tentative date for resumption.{{Cite web|url=https://www.eluniverso.com/deportes/2020/07/13/nota/7905102/ligapro-clubes-autorizados-entrenamientos-colectivos|title=Clubes de LigaPro inician entrenamientos colectivos, reanudación del torneo se mantiene para el 29 de julio|website=El Universo|language=es|date=13 July 2020}} On 27 July, the National COE approved LigaPro's biosecurity protocol and established 15 August as the tentative date to resume the competition.{{Cite web|url=https://www.eluniverso.com/deportes/2020/07/28/nota/7922076/coe-liga-pro-futbol-ecuatoriano-loor-salazar-15-agosto-protocolo|title=COE Nacional aprueba protocolo de bioseguridad de LigaPro y establece fecha tentativa para reinicio del campeonato|website=El Universo|language=es|date=28 July 2020|access-date=29 July 2020}} Eventually, on 11 August the National COE approved LigaPro's request to resume the competition on 14 August, with the completion of the fifth matchday.{{Cite web|url=https://www.eluniverso.com/deportes/2020/08/11/nota/7938397/ligapro-oficial-reanudacion-14-agosto|title=Luz verde para reactivación de la LigaPro, COE Nacional aprobó el 14 de agosto para el
